entry.title: TerminalFix Uses Fake Cloudflare CAPTCHAs to Deploy Reverse-Tunnel Backdoor
entry.content:
red-team · social-engineering

TerminalFix is a ClickFix variant that uses fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA prompts to socially engineer users into executing malicious commands in Windows Terminal or PowerShell, ultimately deploying a reverse-tunnel backdoor. This technique increases effectiveness over traditional ClickFix by leveraging terminal applications to execute complex payloads that Run dialogs cannot handle. Severity is moderate-to-high as it enables backdoor installation and is actively exploited in the wild through social engineering. Recommended actions include user awareness training on suspicious CAPTCHA prompts outside normal browser contexts, blocking execution policies via Group Policy where feasible, and monitoring for suspicious terminal/PowerShell command execution patterns.

entry.title: Klever: Integer overflow in split-royalty validation enables unbounded minting of KLV (native token) (CVE-2026-54755)
entry.content:
vulnerability · integer-overflow · CVE-2026-54755

Klever Go SDK's split-royalty validation contains a critical integer overflow vulnerability in the uint32 accumulator used to verify per-entry percentages (CVE-2026-54755). An attacker can craft two split entries with percentages summing over 2^32 to bypass validation while storing astronomically large individual values, enabling unbounded minting of KLV tokens during royalty payout. This is critical severity with no current indication of wild exploitation but represents complete loss of token supply integrity. Immediate patching required: upgrade to a fixed version that implements proper bounds checking on individual percentage entries before accumulation or uses uint64 for accumulator validation.

entry.content:

Yamcs (org.yamcs:yamcs-core) contains a critical authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in StreamSQL `LIKE` operator handling. User-supplied LIKE patterns are inserted unescaped into Java code compiled by Janino, allowing an attacker to break out of string literals and inject arbitrary Java code (such as static blocks executing OS commands) when the compiled filter class loads. The vulnerability affects all versions and is exploitable by authenticated users; no public exploitation in the wild has been reported yet. Patch immediately by upgrading to a patched version when available, or apply input validation/escaping for LIKE patterns as a temporary mitigation.

entry.content:
vulnerability · insufficient-entropy · CVE-2026-71851

CryptoJS library versions containing `WordArray.random()` suffer from insufficient entropy in cryptographic secret generation, producing only ~2^39 bits of effective entropy for 128-bit requests and ~2^47 for 256-bit requests instead of the full keyspace. This vulnerability is critical as it allows attackers to enumerate possible cryptographic secrets on commodity hardware, and is exploited in the wild with downstream wallet applications using the function for BIP39 recovery phrase generation. Immediate action required: update CryptoJS to a patched version and audit any applications using this library for key generation, particularly cryptocurrency wallets and sensitive credential systems, regenerating compromised secrets.

entry.title: Living off the coding agent: Two tales of tunnels and LaunchAgents
entry.content:
red-team · lateral-movement

macOS LaunchAgents and agent-generated reverse tunnels can enable local admin applications to be exposed to the internet, creating unauthorized remote access pathways. This technique exploits legitimate system automation features to establish persistence and external connectivity without requiring traditional malware signatures, making detection difficult for endpoint tools. The severity is high due to potential for unauthorized system access and lateral movement, though exploitation in the wild remains tied to targeted operations rather than mass campaigns. Organizations should implement strict LaunchAgent monitoring, restrict outbound tunnel creation, enforce network segmentation for admin applications, and treat suspicious reverse tunnel activity as security incidents regardless of whether it appears to be "vibe-coded" rather than confirmed malicious.

entry.title: Craft CMS: Passkey login accepts replayed WebAuthn assertions
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass

Craft CMS 5.10.3 and earlier versions contain a critical vulnerability in passkey/WebAuthn login that accepts user-supplied `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions` and fails to update stored credential counters, allowing captured login requests to be replayed indefinitely. An unauthenticated attacker who obtains a single passkey assertion can authenticate as the victim by replaying the captured request, bypassing WebAuthn's replay protection mechanism. This vulnerability is likely exploitable in the wild given its straightforward nature. Immediately upgrade to a patched version and audit login logs for suspicious WebAuthn activity; consider temporarily disabling passkey authentication until patching is completed.

entry.content:

Update immediately to patched stable kernels (7.1.6, 6.18.42, 6.12.101, or 6.6.148 released August 3, 2024), or disable SCTP if the protocol is not required in your environment. Prioritize systems where untrusted users have local access or where containerization is deployed.

entry.title: Traefik: Authentication Bypass via Path Traversal in ReplacePathRegex Middleware (CVE-2026-65600)
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass · CVE-2026-65600

Traefik's ReplacePathRegex middleware contains a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-65600) where improperly configured regex replacements allow path traversal attacks to bypass security controls. Crafted requests can generate unnormalized paths like `/../admin` that forward to backends without validation, potentially exposing protected resources when the backend normalizes the path. This affects Traefik v2 and v3. Users must update to patched versions and review ReplacePathRegex configurations to ensure regex patterns include mandatory separators between captured segments; consider alternative middleware if traversal patterns are unavoidable.

Severity is high as it defeats current protections, though wild exploitation likelihood is currently unknown given the technical sophistication required. Mitigation requires updated CPU microcode and kernel patches; users should monitor vendor advisories from Intel, AMD, and Linux distributions for available fixes and apply them promptly.

entry.title: New Zapscape KVM Flaw Could Let Privileged L1 Guest Code Escape to Linux Hosts
entry.content:
vulnerability · vm-escape · CVE-2026-64561

Zapscape (CVE-2026-64561) is a privilege escalation vulnerability in Linux KVM/x86's shadow MMU that allows an attacker with kernel-level access in a nested L1 guest VM to escape to the host system. The flaw affects systems with nested virtualization enabled and exposed to untrusted guests; severity is high due to escape from isolation boundary but exploitation requires pre-existing kernel privileges within guest. A kernel patch addressing the shadow MMU handling is required; systems should disable nested virtualization for untrusted workloads until patched. No evidence of in-the-wild exploitation reported at this time.
